comment: Frozen render-check expectations. M3 task 3 (iter 44) froze the
vfx/overlay-BLIND reduced-sequence pin at 0.91; that pin RETIRED
WITH the exposure it measured when M4 task 2 (iter 65) extended the
sequence to include renderVfx()+renderOverlay(true) on BOTH sides
(mask widened fg1|fg2 -> fg1|fg2|UI). New-pin procedure (iter-65
pre-registration): threshold SEEDED at 0.85 BEFORE the first
vfx-inclusive pass (text glyphs + boundary-heavy vfx add browser-
side AA dilation classes the C 0.2-px plane cannot dilate into);
after the first honest run, frozen at floor(min*100)/100 when
min > seed. MEASURED (iter 65): honest run 1 min 0.8970 (f3599) /
max 0.9846 (f0100); a provisional 0.89 freeze was then REFUTED by
the cold run's fresh capture (f1297 0.8835) — root-caused to
percentShake, the wall-clock timing-dependent exclusion, varying
capture-to-capture. ONE bounded methodology round (the
pre-registered refutation shape (a)): the capture's render guard
now zeroes percentShake (snapshot/restore; C draws unshaken, so the
pairing is honest on both sides), and the threshold is FROZEN at
0.88 = floor over BOTH honest measurements' minima, BEFORE the
first passing done-check. NEVER loosened from here (CLAUDE.md hard
rule 3; PROCESS.md section 8).
HISTORICAL — the paragraph above narrates the RETIRED 0.88 freeze,
and the residual list it relied on is NO LONGER CURRENT. It said the
residual cross-capture variance was 'render-plane RNG scatter only'
and listed 'render-plane RNG divergence (star scatter, tail jitter,
electrichit lightning: same shapes, different samples)' among the
residuals the threshold absorbs. C28 (review-134) removed that cause
entirely: the browser render plane now draws from a page-local
mulberry32 chained in step with the C's render RNG, not native
Math.random, and measuredAtFreeze below records a run-to-run spread
of 0.0000 over 6 fresh captures. Do NOT re-derive slack from the
retired list (independent-reviewer Low, review-134): the residuals
that are STILL LIVE and still absorbed by the fg threshold are
percentShake (native-RNG + wall-clock decay; zeroed by the capture's
render guard, C draws unshaken), screenShake fg1 transients, and
canvas AA / text-boundary dilation — which is the AA fringe the
0.92 bound was measured against.
Corpus (reviewed pin change, 16 -> 24 g01 frames, iter 65): the
frozen 16 (30 ENTRANCE+Ready, 100 post-GO, 170 laser, 971 GUARD,
1234 KO flight, 1237 first DEAD*, 1297 REBIRTH, 2552 DAMAGE*, fills
seeded circleDust live), 150 (injection frame), 184 (normalhit t2 +
laser muzzle t3), 426 (marth swing trail), 1238 (blastzone t2),
2277 (doubleJumpRings t3), 2807 (hitSparks/hitFlair t2), 2956
(tech t2). sampledFrameCount is pinned here + check-render.sh +
iou.js (the three twin pins).
inject: the synthetic-coverage table (iter-65 pre-registration).
firefoxcharge/firefoxlaunch/shine/shineloop have ZERO live frames
in EVERY golden (measured across the iter-64 captures), and Chase's
playtest saw firefox+shine missing — so the SAME configs spawn on
BOTH sides at frame 150 (measured vfx-quiet: entrance <= 60, start
<= 120, laser >= 172, swing >= 424), after the tick's spawns and
before the render. None of the injected names draw seeded RNG at
spawn; every capture stays STREAM-MATCH gated. firefoxlaunch/
shineloop are PLAYER-STATE-GATED upstream (actionState
UPSPECIALLAUNCH / player.shineLoop), so both sides draw NOTHING on
a non-upspecial frame: injected as no-crash structural coverage,
honestly stated as visually UNVERIFIED here; visual authority =
task-3's device rung + Chase's M4 playthrough.
injectPin (iter 67, review-65 M1): the REVIEWED injection set,
frozen — names in inject.configs order, count, frame, and the
inkNames subset (the five effects that DRAW on a plain frame; the
gated firefoxlaunch/shineloop pair stays structural-only).
check-render.sh (early + at the INJECT1 emitter), capture-canvas.js
(pre-browser) and iou.js (the judge) each independently assert the
runtime inject table == this pin (exact ordered names, uniqueness,
count, frame identity, frame in sampledFrames) — a dropped/renamed
effect is a loud pin death, never a silent both-sides omission.
Per-effect ink assertions (iter 67, review-65 M2): at inject.frame
iou.js asserts, for every inkNames effect, nonzero browser-mask ink
AND nonzero C ink AND nonzero C DIFFERENTIAL ink (with-inject vs
the no-inject baseline render) inside the effect's derived region,
plus the soundness guard that every differential pixel falls inside
the union of derived regions. Region derivation documented in
iou.js (executed stages.json transform + frozen VFXDATA1 template
bounds x upstream dVfx code-literal scales). Aggregate IoU stays
the frame-level judge; these are per-effect existence tripwires.
Round-2 hardening (iter 70, review-65 r2): inkNames is HARD-pinned
(exact ordered 5-name set) in check-render.sh, capture-canvas.js
and iou.js — changing the set is a reviewed 4-file change. The
capture additionally records, at inject.frame only, deterministic
browser masks (f0150.det.mask.bin + f0150.loo-<name>.mask.bin, a
page-local mulberry32 swapped in per render, gameplay chain
untouched) and iou.js asserts per-effect browser LEAVE-ONE-OUT
differential ink (bdiff) > 0 — browser-side attribution, the twin
of the C leave-one-out. firefoxcharge's judge region derives from
cfg.f (the drawn frame index; face is the mirror flag) — frames
3/7 per the drawVfx f->facing mapping.
Round-3 hardening (iter 71, review-70 r3): the injection-frame
CANONICAL render joined the deterministic render-plane RNG (same
page-local mulberry32/seed as det/loo) and the det mask is a
strict replay of it, asserted byte-identical capture-side AND
judge-side; the extra det/loo renders are side-effect-free
observations (post-canonical vfxQueue restored by reference, no
finally re-render, zero native draws at the frame) so frames 151+
continue exactly the trajectory the saved f0150 mask shows. The
old native canonical + finally re-render left the mask on
trajectory A while the queue continued on B (measured: randomTail
0/4 components equal, .loop/m4-task2r71-probe-old.log). No pinned
value changed; f0150's IoU sample stream moved from native to the
det seed (same distribution).
Methodology pins (iou.js implements these; changing any is a
methodology change and requires re-freezing BEFORE judgment, never
after): browser mask = fg1|fg2|UI alpha>0 at 1200x750, downscaled
5x5 any-ink to 240x150; C mask = the rasterizer ink plane (PGM) in
the letterbox band rows [45,195), zero C ink allowed outside (the C
background pass is ink-suppressed); retarget k=0.2 dy=45;
IoU >= iouThreshold per frame.
servedDistSha256: REPINNED by U1 (the served main.js now carries the two extra background hooks); consoleErrorAllowlist unchanged (M3 task 3
provenance — see git history for the full derivation notes).

BYTE-IDENTICAL between the Chrome-150 cold run .loop/render-r4.log and

THRESHOLD differs, by design: the ART bound was tightened this round).
PROVENANCE NOTE (r6 M3 — a stale citation this round had to correct):
the comparison is deliberately anchored to those two RUN LOGS, which
are append-only session artifacts, and NOT to
.loop/review-134-regression/cand.out, which an earlier draft of this
note cited. That corpus is REPUBLISHED from the current build output on
every successful regression run, so it now holds Chrome-151 bytes and
cannot evidence anything about 150. Chrome 150 is no longer installed
on the host and is not reacquirable; the durable logs above are the
surviving 150 evidence, and the rig now stamps every published corpus
with the engine that produced it so this cannot recur silently.
This is an ENGINE-IDENTITY re-pin with measured zero metric movement;
it is NOT a widened bound, and the accompanying ART bound change in

Spread evidence: .loop/render-chrome151-measure.log (capture 1) + the

2026-08-05 (driver): CHANNEL ONLY, 'chrome' -> 'chrome-for-testing'.
The VERSION is UNCHANGED and still exact (151.0.7922.71) and NO BOUND
was touched: this is NOT a re-measure and makes no metric claim.
Cause: channel 'chrome' resolves to whatever Google Chrome the host
happens to have, the host auto-updated to 151.0.7922.76, and the pin
then fired on every run so NO capture of any kind could be taken
(.loop/a14-render1.log). Re-measuring on each Chrome update would make
these frozen bounds a function of the developer's browser update
schedule. Chrome for Testing publishes THIS EXACT BUILD immutably and
never self-updates, so the engine stops being ambient state.
The pin is STRICTER after this change, not looser: it names an exact
BINARY (executablePath, existence asserted, no fallback launch) in
addition to the exact version. The re-measure protocol in `note` below
is UNCHANGED and still binds any future VERSION move.
note: review-134 r1 M1. Every bound in this file is a measured property of
ONE rasterizer: the capture used to try channel 'chrome' and SILENTLY
fall back to Playwright's bundled Chromium, and both report
browserType().name() == 'chromium', so a capture could be produced by
an engine nobody measured while the source closure looked identical.
capture-canvas.js now launches exactly one engine with no fallback and
asserts this pin live; check-render.sh asserts it against the sidecar,
which covers MLFK_GFX_REUSE_CANVAS (that mode launches no browser at
all, so it is precisely where the identity would otherwise be unknown).
EXACT version, not a major-version prefix (review-134 r2 M1): Skia
rasterization changes at PATCH level, and the fg margin is 0.0008 IoU
(0.9208 measured MIN against the 0.92 bound) = about 3 device cells at
~0.00026 IoU per cell on that frame, so a '15x.*' prefix would have let
an unmeasured rasterizer through while the check still claimed to fail
closed on an update. (The 150 -> 151 re-measurement above happens to
have moved nothing; that is a MEASURED outcome of one update, not a
licence to weaken the pin to a prefix.)
WHEN THIS FIRES (any Chrome update), that is correct behaviour.
Re-measure — >=6 fresh captures, record the spread — and re-freeze this
version plus any bound that actually moved. NEVER widen a bound to
silence it.
U3 freeze, iter 134. The fg IoU is an aggregate and could not see
articles at all: a C build with renderArticles stubbed out entirely
scored IOU MIN 0.9143 against the 0.88 fg bound and exited 0
(MEASURED — third instance of U1's class). This plane draws the
article pass ALONE on both sides (gfx_render.c article sink /
gfx-pagelib.js __gfxArticlePlane), so removing articles scores 0.
WHY 0.66 AND NOT 0.95: the disagreement is entirely a <=1-device-
cell antialiasing fringe, MEASURED both directions — the C plane is
a strict SUBSET of the browser plane on all four frames (inter ==
C cells exactly), and the browser plane is entirely covered by the
C plane dilated by ONE cell (0 uncovered cells, all four frames).
Chrome inks every pixel a 0.8-alpha 'screen' laser quad touches;
the C rasterizer inks a tighter footprint. On a 79-82 cell plane
that fringe is ~30% of the union, so 0.66 is what an EXACTLY
correct laser scores here, not slack. The plane is small, so one
cell is ~0.0126 IoU on the MIN frame.
THE BOUND IS NOW PER-FRAME (artFrameFloors), NOT A SINGLE GLOBAL
FLOOR (codex r6 M1 — and it was RIGHT). A global floor can only be
calibrated on ONE frame; calibrated on the MIN frame it leaves
progressively MORE slack on every higher-scoring frame. Measured at
the 0.645 global floor: f0184 (56/82 = 0.6829) still PASSED with
THREE cells missing (53/82 = 0.6463) and with FOUR cells invented
(56/86 = 0.6512). Each frame now carries its own floor, derived the
same way for all four: admit exactly ONE device cell of movement in
either direction, reject TWO. Since the C plane is a strict subset of
the browser plane, a MISSING cell costs the intersection ((i-1)/u)
and an INVENTED one costs the union (i/(u+1)), so each floor sits in
the half-open window ( max(2-missing, 2-spurious), min(1-missing,
1-spurious) ] and is the truncated top of it:
f1237 and f1238 52/79 -> 0.6455. EVERY frame is toothed in BOTH
directions, not just the min one (.loop/review-134-r5-teeth.log).
History: the first bound was a global 0.63; the independent reviewer
showed it admitted a 2-cell-short laser on the min frame and it was
tightened to a global 0.645; r6 then showed the global shape itself
was the defect. NEVER widen any of these: a fired ART frame means
that frame's laser silhouette moved.
The superseded global-floor rationale, kept because it records the
measurement: 0.63 was reserved
'about two cells of environment margin', which is the very basis r3
M4 had just rejected for the fg bound: the measured movement of THIS
plane is 0.0000 on every axis anyone has measured it on — byte-
identical across 6 fresh captures on Chrome 150, byte-identical
across 6 more on Chrome 151, 0.0000 across the --disable-gpu
--disable-accelerated-2d-canvas rasterizer-backend change, and
0.0000 across the 150 -> 151 engine update. Reserved cells with no
measured cause are exactly what U3 was filed about.
WHAT THE OLD SLACK BOUGHT A WRONG RENDERER (computed on the MIN
frame f1237/f1238, browser 79 cells, C 52, C a strict subset so a
missing cell costs the intersection and a spurious cell costs the
union): at 0.63 the leg still PASSED with 2 of the laser's cells
MISSING (50/79 = 0.6329) or with 3 cells INVENTED outside the
browser plane (52/82 = 0.6341) — a 4-6% shape tolerance on the only
leg that can see articles at all. At 0.645 exactly ONE cell of
movement in either direction is admitted and TWO is rejected:
1 missing 51/79 = 0.6456 PASS, 2 missing 0.6329 FAIL; 1 spurious
52/80 = 0.6500 PASS, 2 spurious 52/81 = 0.6420 FAIL. Verified
against the pinned archived corpus with the candidate judge.
0.645 keeps 0.0132 of margin under the measured 0.6582 min = ~1.05
cells, i.e. one cell more tolerance than any movement ever measured
on this plane; 0.65 would reject even a single AA cell, so this is
the tightest bound that is still a bound and not a bit-compare.
NEVER widen it: a fired ART leg means the laser silhouette moved.
Registered, NOT fixed here: the same AA-fringe signature
dominates the aggregate fg leg (browser-only cells outnumber
C-only ~6:1 on quiet frames) — a rasterizer-coverage question, not
an article question.
Both sides were byte-identical across two independent fresh
captures, so the run-to-run noise floor on this plane is 0.
U1 freeze, 2026-07-28. Both bg legs are deterministic on BOTH sides
(gfx-pagelib.js __gfxBgInit mirrors gfx_bg.c's render-local
mulberry32 and start state), so these are geometry numbers, not
statistics. stars ~0.995+: the starfield and both mountain beziers

BUT thin strokes (16 rays lineWidth 2 + 5 rings lineWidth 1..10

note: C28 re-freeze, iter 134. The 0.88 bound could not be tightened
because the METRIC ITSELF drifted: the browser reference render
consumed V8's native Math.random, so every RNG-consuming vfx
landed somewhere else in every capture. MEASURED before the fix:
5 of the 24 sampled fg masks differed between two otherwise
identical captures (f0030 2288 source px, f0184 1160, f1234 1015,
f2956 80, f0076 1) while every seeded-stream plane (bg / star /
tunnel / gradient / det / loo) was byte-identical — and seven
distinct IOU MIN values in 0.9004-0.9076 had been observed from
identical code.
FIX: the render plane runs on a page-local mulberry32 seeded with
0xC0FFEE42 — the SAME render-local stream and seed gfx_vfx.c
already chains (gfx_vfx_install), chained the same way, since both
sides render every frame. Not window.__nativeRandom: percentShake
draws from that from wall-clock setTimeout callbacks.
CONTROL (disambiguation, PROCESS 7.5): the same deterministic
machinery seeded 0xDEADBEEF instead scores IOU MIN 0.9058, so the
0.9025 -> 0.9208 rise is real stream ALIGNMENT with the C, not an
artifact of determinism.
NOISE FLOOR: 6 independent fresh captures produced BYTE-IDENTICAL
judge output on every leg and every frame (spread 0.0000). The
only capture-side variation seen at all is one antialiased source
pixel at (852,339) that flipped in 1 of 8 captures and changed no
device cell (the known glyph-jitter class, glyphComparePins).
MARGIN: 0.92, i.e. 0.0008 below the measured min = about 3 device
cells of the 3,863-cell min-frame union. It is MEASURED, not
reserved (review-134 r3 M4 rejected the earlier 0.915 as an
unmeasured allowance: the exact browser-version pin already rejects
every different Chrome build, so "cross-build drift" could not
justify a margin).
The measurement is a CONTROLLED same-version environment change —
the same Chrome 150.0.7871.187, relaunched with --disable-gpu
--disable-accelerated-2d-canvas, i.e. a different rasterizer backend:
* all 19 frames scoring below 0.94 (the ones a bound near 0.92
actually judges) moved by at most 0.0003, and the MIN frame
* the single larger excursion is f0030 at -0.0086 — the ready/go
BANNER frame, which scores 0.9652, five points clear of the
bound, and is the text-AA case glyphComparePins already
documents;
* the ARTICLE plane moved by 0.0000 on all four frames.
So 0.0008 is ~3x the largest movement measured on any frame the bound
can judge. Tightening further would start judging single-cell AA
noise (1 device cell on the min frame is ~0.00026 IoU).
RESIDUAL, registered: the disagreement that remains is dominated
by a <=1-cell antialiasing fringe — on quiet frames browser-only
cells outnumber C-only ~6:1 (f0184: 321 vs 50). That is a
rasterizer-coverage question and is why the fg bound is 0.92 and
not 0.99; it is not run-to-run noise.
